transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. It's probably nothing too terrible, really, but... well, I guess I just don’t have the push I used to have. 

I used to always be doing something, you know? Choir, my quilting, or just going out and visiting folks. But lately, I just... I mostly just sit at home all day with the TV on real low. I know people are expecting me at these things, and I feel just awful about letting them down, but I just can't seem to get going. I want to be good about it and do what I'm supposed to, I really do. 

Is... is that an okay reason to come see you? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time lately?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around crying or feeling sorry for myself, because I'm really not. I have a lot to be thankful for, I truly do. 

It's not sadness, and I don't feel... empty, exactly. I just feel kind of... well, just still, I suppose. I'm not unhappy, I just can't seem to muster up the energy to do my usual things. I hope I'm explaining that right... does that make sense, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Do you find that you're not enjoying the things you used to enjoy?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I don't enjoy them anymore. I mean, I love my quilting group, and singing in the choir is always such a blessing. I wouldn't want anyone to think I don't appreciate those things, because I really do. 

It's just... when I'm actually doing them, I suppose I don't get that same little spark I used to get. It's not that I dislike it, it's just... a bit flat, maybe? But I still think they're wonderful activities. I hope that doesn't sound ungrateful. Is it alright if I feel that way sometimes?
Do you feel like you're looking forward to things less often than you used to?

Well, I suppose... maybe a little bit less? But I don't want you to think I'm a pessimist or anything like that. I still look forward to seeing my grandchildren, of course, and I always hope for good weather. 

I guess I just don't have that same... excitement bubbling up for the everyday things like I used to. But I know everyone slows down a little at my age, right? That's just normal, isn't it? I just want to be sure I'm not making a fuss over something that's perfectly fine.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to find pleasure in?

Oh, goodness, no, I wouldn't say I've lost interest. I still care very much about my little projects and my family. I don't want you to think I've just given up or that I'm sitting around being lazy, because I certainly haven't. 

I still want to be involved in things, truly I do. I try my very best to keep busy. I think it's so important to stay active and be a good member of the community, don't you? I'm trying to do exactly what I'm supposed to do, just keeping on with things as best I can. I hope I'm being helpful to you today with these answers... am I doing alright, Doctor?
Do you often feel tired?

Oh, tired? Well, no, I... I wouldn't say I'm tired all the time. I make sure to get up and do my chores every morning. I don't want to be one of those people who just sleeps the day away, you know? I try very hard to keep my energy up. 

I mean, maybe by the evening I'm a little worn out, but... well, at sixty-seven, needing a little rest after supper is perfectly acceptable, isn't it? I'm certainly not trying to complain about my energy or anything. I just try to do my fair share around the house. I hope that's alright to say, Doctor. I'm doing okay with that, aren't I?
Have you noticed any change in your appetite lately?

Oh, my appetite? Well, no, I... I eat just fine, really I do. I always make sure to finish what's on my plate. I know how important it is to keep your strength up, and I certainly don't want to be fussy about my meals or waste good food. 

I try to eat my regular portions every day, just exactly like you're supposed to. I haven't noticed it going up or down or anything like that. I hope that's a good sign... it's good that I'm still eating well, isn't it, Doctor?
Do you often feel guilty about not doing things you used to do?

Guilty? Oh, heavens, no. I don't feel guilty. I... I do what I can, you know? I still keep up with the things that matter most, and I certainly don't sit around feeling sorry for myself or dwelling on things I can't do anymore. 

I mean, everyone slows down a little bit at my age, right? It's just natural. I try to focus on being useful where I am needed now, instead of worrying about the past. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting here feeling bad about myself, because I'm not. I'm keeping a very positive attitude about it all. That's the right way to look at it, isn't it, Doctor?
Do you feel like you're getting as much pleasure out of the things you're still doing as you used to?

Oh, pleasure? Yes, absolutely. I... I still enjoy my days very much. I make sure to appreciate the little things, you know? Just... keeping things tidy or having a nice cup of tea in the afternoon. 

I certainly don't sit around moping or finding fault with everything. I think it's so important to stay cheerful and be grateful for what you have, rather than complaining. I'm doing my best to keep a smile on my face, Doctor. I'm doing the right thing by staying upbeat, aren't I?
Have you noticed any change in how quickly or slowly you move compared to how you used to?

Oh, my moving? No, I... I get around just fine, I really do. I make sure to keep myself busy and get my chores done every day. I certainly don't just sit around like a bump on a log, expecting people to wait on me. 

I know some folks my age get real slow and start dragging their feet, but I try very hard to keep a good, steady pace. I keep up with everything just exactly like I always have. I'm doing my absolute best to stay active and not be a burden to anybody... staying on your feet and keeping busy is the best way to be, isn't it, Doctor?
Do you feel like things that used to give you pleasure, now feel less enjoyable to you?

Less enjoyable? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I still find plenty of joy in my day-to-day routine. I... I make sure to appreciate the little things, you know? Like I said, a nice cup of tea, or just keeping the house neat. 

I'm certainly not one of those people who just stops caring about everything. I think it's so important to keep finding the good in things, don't you? I try very hard to stay positive and not let myself get down in the dumps. I'm doing a good job of keeping my spirits up, aren't I, Doctor?
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that you used to find enjoyable?

Oh, no, Doctor. I... well, like I was saying just a minute ago, I really do still enjoy things just fine. I promise I haven't lost my ability to smile. I still like doing the things I always did, honest. 

I'm not giving up or letting myself go... I swear it. I try very hard to be a happy person and appreciate the good Lord's blessings. You don't have to worry about me being ungrateful or anything like that. I'm doing okay, aren't I? I just hope I'm answering all these questions right for you.
Do you feel like you have to push yourself to do things that you used to do without thinking?

Well, I... I suppose I might have to push just a little bit more than I used to. But that's just getting older, isn't it? It's perfectly normal to need a minute to get going. 

I mean, I still do things. But... well, to be perfectly honest, I haven't been keeping up with choir or my quilting quite as much lately. And I know the ladies expect me for our visits, but sometimes I just... I end up sitting at home. I keep the TV on, just real low for company. 

I know I shouldn't be staying in so much, and I feel just awful when I let people down. I don't want you to think I'm lazy, Doctor. I really am trying to be better about it. It's just... the push I used to have, it's a little harder to find right now. That doesn't make me a bad person, does it?
Do you feel like you have lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, even if you still participate in them?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I've completely lost interest. I really don't want to sound like I don't care about things anymore. I still think choir and my quilting group are wonderful, and I love the ladies. 

It's just like I was saying before... I just don't have that same push I used to have for them. I know they expect me, and I feel terrible when I don't go. But most days, I just end up sitting at home with the TV on low. I guess I'm still participating in my own way, just... quietly? 

I really hope you don't think I'm just giving up on everything. I'm trying my best to stay involved when I can. That's alright, isn't it? I mean, it's okay to need a little more quiet time at my age, right?
Do you feel like you have lost interest in the activities you used to enjoy, even if it's just a little bit?

Well, I... I guess if I'm being perfectly honest, maybe just a tiny bit? I don't want you to think I'm ungrateful or that I don't care about my friends. The ladies are so good to me. 

But like I mentioned, I just... I don't have that same push I used to have for choir or the quilting. And visiting folks... I know they expect me, and I feel just awful when I don't show up. But most days, I just end up sitting at home with the TV on low. 

I'm not doing it on purpose, I promise. It's just... maybe I have lost a little bit of the spark for it right now. But I'm going to try harder, I really am. You don't think terribly of me for that, do you, Doctor? It's just a little phase, I'm sure.
Do you feel like you're unable to feel happy or get pleasure from things that normally would make you happy?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I can't feel happy at all. I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself or being miserable. I always try to count my blessings. 

But... I suppose it goes back to what I was saying before. The things that always brought me so much joy, like the choir or my quilting, or going out visiting folks... I just don't have the push for them right now. Even when I think about how much I used to love it, that... that warm, happy feeling is just a little hard to find. 

So I just end up sitting at home with the TV on low, even though I know the ladies are expecting me to be there, smiling and joining in. I feel just terrible that I'm not getting the same joy out of it right now. I'm trying to look on the bright side, though, I really am. I hope I'm explaining this right for you, Doctor. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling like you don't have the push to do things you used to enjoy?

Well, I... I suppose it hasn't been a sudden thing. I wouldn't want you to think I just woke up one day and decided to stop trying. It's been more of a... a gradual slowing down, I guess you could say. 

It started building up after I retired from the school office. That was a little over two years ago now. I was so used to being busy and helpful there, you know? And since then, it's just been a bit harder to find that same energy. But two years isn't so long to adjust to a big change like retirement, is it? I mean, it's perfectly normal to take a little time to find your footing again, don't you think? I'm sure I'll bounce back soon.
How many months would you say you've been feeling like you don't have the push to do things you used to enjoy?

Oh, I'm sorry, Doctor, I should have figured that out for you a moment ago. I didn't mean to make you ask twice. Let me think... well, two years is twenty-four months, isn't it? And since it's been a little over two years since I finished up at the school office, I suppose it would be... maybe twenty-five or twenty-six months? 

I know when you count it all up in months like that, it sounds like an awfully long time to be lacking that push. I hope you don't think I've just been giving up all those months. I really have been trying to keep a good attitude and do what I can. Is twenty-five or twenty-six months the kind of answer you needed? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Would you say this lack of push has been going on for less than 6 months?

Oh, my, I must have completely confused you, Doctor. I am so sorry about that, I really didn't mean to mix you up. No, it's... it's been quite a bit longer than six months. 

Like I was trying to say just a moment ago, this whole feeling has been building up since I retired from the school office... which was a little over two years ago. I must not have been very clear before, and I apologize for making you ask again. I hope I'm not making your job harder by not explaining things right. Did I clear that up for you now?
Would you say this lack of push has been going on for less than 2 months?

Oh, goodness... no, Doctor, not two months. I'm so sorry, I feel terrible that I keep confusing you. I must be doing a really poor job of explaining myself, and I don't want you to think I'm being difficult on purpose. 

It's... it's definitely been longer than two months. Like I mentioned, it's been a little over two years now, ever since I left my job at the school office. I really hope I haven't frustrated you with all this back and forth. I'm just trying my best to give you the right answers. Does that make more sense now, or should I try to explain it differently?
